summary: # CLO 2024.2 - Hair Cluster Generator In this video, we will explore the features of the Hair Cluster Generator introduced in the CLO Version 2024.2. This tool enhances the user experience by allowing for the creation and self-definition of various hair loss results. ## Introduction to Hair Loss Vinegar Generator To simplify the process of generating hair loss results, we launched the Hair Loss Vinegar Generator. Users can easily self-define and generate multiple hair loss results. Additionally, we have provided 15 pre-set hair loss predictions in the Connect Business City for immediate use. ### Opening the Project File 1. Open the project file. 2. Drag the hair loss prediction—either adjusted from Connect or pre-adjusted by yourself—into the object window and apply it on the board. 3. Select the hair loss material. ### Setting Basic Parameters In the property editor, basic parameters such as hair material and hair type should be set before opening the Hair Loss Generator. ### Accessing the Hair Loss Generator - Scroll down to find the default image. - Click on the hair loss option next to the default image to open the Hair Loss Generator window. ## Hair Loss Generator Overview The Hair Loss Generator features two default images: the long-distance image and the curved-direction image. ### Adjusting Default Images - Click on the long-distance image and the curved-direction image to view their previews. - On the left, you will see the corresponding default preview effect, while the right side displays adjustable attributes. ## Length Chart Adjustments ### Length Chart Attributes Under the attributes on the right of the Length Chart, you will find two attributes: the Cutting Chart and the Editing Effect. If these attributes are not visible, click on the small triangle on the left to reveal them. 1. **Cutting Chart**: Displays different lengths of hair in the same texture pattern. It contains four parameters: mode, image level, low area length, and high area length. Currently, these parameters may be grayed out, indicating a need for adjustments. #### Understanding the Cutting Chart Parameters - **Mode**: Options include RGB and Alpha modes. - **RGB Mode**: The hair length correlates with the grayness of the cutting chart. Black indicates the shortest hair length, while white indicates the longest. - **Alpha Mode**: Hair length depends on transparency. Transparent areas indicate the shortest hair, and non-transparent areas indicate the longest. - **Image Level**: Adjusts the intensity of gray. Increasing this value enhances the cut effect. - **Low Area Length & High Area Length**: Adjusts the shortest and longest hair lengths, respectively. ### Editing Effect Parameters The Editing Effect includes two parameters: intensity and randomness. - **Intensity**: A higher intensity value results in a more pronounced difference in hair length from the edge to the center, creating a sharper appearance. - **Randomness**: Adjusts the consistency or irregularity of hair length across the fabric's surface. A higher value leads to a more chaotic distribution of hair lengths. ## Curve Direction Adjustments ### Curve Direction Chart Properties The Curve Direction Chart includes the properties of Hair Loss and Hair Loss Details. 1. **Hair Loss**: This property simulates the effect of individual hairs. It consists of the following parameters: - **Intensity**: Adjusts the visibility of each hair's direction. Higher values create a more pronounced three-dimensional effect. - **Hair Loss Density**: Higher values result in a denser appearance of hair loss. - **Random Direction & Random Intensity**: Determines whether the curve direction is consistent or irregular. 2. **Hair Loss Details**: Used to fine-tune the detail effect of each hair loss instance. It includes five parameters, similar to those described above. ### Adjusting Hair Loss Parameters - **Intensity of Hair Loss**: Adjusts the concentration of hair loss while maintaining directionality. Higher values result in smoother and more loosely styled hair. ## Practical Application Adjustments ### Adjusting Hair Loss Effects To adjust the hair loss effect based on the preview: 1. Open the Length Chart. 2. Since this hair loss effect does not require different lengths, the Cutting Chart is unnecessary. 3. Adjust the strength to a value of 0.3 for sharper edges. 4. Set the length rule to a value of 0.08. ### Adjusting Bend Direction 1. Set the strength value for the bend direction to 0.45. 2. Adjust the density of the hair vinegar to 0.2. 3. Keep the bending direction and bending strength at 0 or adjust to 0.05. ### Hair Loss Details Adjustments 1. Adjust the detail effect based on the desired outcome. 2. Set the looseness to 0.45 for a slightly open appearance. ### Finalizing Adjustments After adjusting each parameter, click on "Apply," then "Close" to save your settings. Finally, open the synchronization rendering window to view the final effect. If satisfied, output the rendering image. ## Creating a Flower-Shaped Hair Effect To create a hair effect with a partial flower shape: 1. Open the Hair Vinegar Generator. 2. Under the Length Image, add a pre-made black and white flower-shaped image (ensure it's a gray image). 3. Select RGB mode for the image. 4. Adjust properties to enhance clarity in the flower-shaped area, such as setting the image level to 0.65 and the low area height to 0.2. 5. Click on "Apply," then "Close," and run synchronization rendering to check the final effect. ## Conclusion We believe that the application of the new Hair Hair Preset and Hair Vinegar Generator by Kinect will significantly enhance your design experience and expand your creative capabilities. We look forward to seeing how you use the Hair Vinegar Generator to experiment with hair designs. Thank you for watching, and see you next time!
